solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First to move the panel, shifting piece of junk

parts.note: in chess the side that moves first is White

indicators.note: shifting means the letters of 'the panel' are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone moving furniture goes first with a panel while shifting an unwanted item out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to move' is not a letter pick: in chess White always moves first. THE PANEL rearranged gives ELEPHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A white elephant is a costly possession that is useless to its owner, a burdensome bit of rubbish.

clue.text: All day without Charlie? Dreadful: I can't put words to that

definitions.text: I can't put words to that

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a whole day without a friend called Charlie, a feeling too awful to describe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a containment signal but is part of the anagram fodder: ALL DAY WITHOUT plus C, all shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what speakers say when they cannot recall the name for a thing, a placeholder expression.

clue.text: Loading spin-drier, one seen in Madagascar

indicators.note: loading means the phrase 'spin-drier' carries the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone loading a spin-drier, apparently spotted in Madagascar.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is a large lemur, a primate found only on the island of Madagascar.

clue.text: Not demanding all the competitors appearing honest?

parts.note: the entry for a race is the full field of competitors
level means honest or straight, as in 'on the level'

explanation.surface: A contest is easy because every competitor seems straightforward and fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry-level work or equipment is basic, suitable for beginners, so it asks little of the user.

clue.text: Secured page nearly dropped

indicators.note: nearly means the word for page loses its final letter

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book
to shed is to drop, as trees shed leaves

explanation.surface: A page that was fastened down almost fell out.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that is leashed is restrained or tied up, held in place by a lead.

clue.text: Feeling for small coin, one to place on drawing

indicators.note: in a down entry, placing one on something puts it above, so it comes first

parts.note: P stands for penny, a small British coin
I is the Roman numeral for one
drawing a match is tying it, finishing level

explanation.surface: An artist feels for a small coin and places one on a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art, but it is the sporting sense: a drawn game is a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitying someone means feeling sympathy or compassion for them in their distress.

clue.text: Aussie PM has a bible, the opposition leader too

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of 'opposition'

explanation.surface: Australia's prime minister owns a Bible, as does the head of the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like Prime Minister in the political surface, but it is post meridiem, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvo is Australian slang for the afternoon, the post meridiem hours.

clue.text: Set among woods, hotel given one rating or another

indicators.note: given means the sailor follows on after the first part
set among means the hotel letter is placed inside the word for woods

parts.note: woods are made up of trees
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a tar is a sailor, and a rating is a non-officer sailor

explanation.surface: A hotel set in woodland receives a review score of one sort or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two senses of rating: TAR is one rating (a sailor), and the answer is another rating, the kind given to hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-star grade is a different kind of rating, a classification for hotels and restaurants.

clue.text: One actor fired perhaps, with nothing written on sort of paper

parts.note: a blank sheet has nothing written on it
cartridge paper is a thick drawing paper

explanation.surface: An actor is sacked, perhaps, with nothing written on a particular kind of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actor fired' suggests a dismissal, but on stage an actor may fire a gun loaded with harmless rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank round contains powder but no bullet, so it is used by performers firing guns in plays.

clue.text: Check temperature on car

indicators.note: in an across clue, temperature on car means it comes after the car

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

explanation.surface: A mechanic checks the temperature reading on a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection or examination, especially of accounts.

clue.text: Not keen on new rival type of drug

parts.note: to be anti something is to be against it

indicators.note: new means the letters of 'rival' are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A drug company is wary of a fresh competitor's medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antivirals are a class of medicines that act against viruses.

clue.text: Period in which one's at home drinking tea; Alice never quite made it

indicators.note: in which means the first part sits inside the period

parts.note: a day is a period of time
I is one, so one's (one is) gives I then S
at home is IN and tea is CHA (slang for tea); read as being at home with tea, the tea comes first

explanation.surface: A day spent at home sipping tea, and Alice could never quite finish the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Alice was wondering whether to make a daisy chain when the White Rabbit ran by and she followed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice was considering threading flowers into a garland when the White Rabbit interrupted, so it was never completed.

clue.text: Farm worker finds nothing in sty

indicators.note: in means the nothing letter goes inside the word for sty

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A farmhand finds the pigsty empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A peon is a Latin American labourer, especially an agricultural one.

clue.text: Permitted variations aren't close when worked out

indicators.note: worked out means the letters of 'aren't close' are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Allowed deviations turn out not to be tight once calculated.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineering tolerances are the allowed margins by which a measurement may differ from its nominal value.

clue.text: Start and finish not clearly defined

parts.note: to open is to start
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A contest whose start and finish are vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no fixed limits or conclusion, so its scope is indefinite.

clue.text: All fine with me, getting changed at home?

indicators.note: getting changed means the letters of 'all fine' and 'me' are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says all is fine with them while dressing at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase en famille means with one's family, in a domestic or informal setting.

clue.text: Having secret knowledge, lied perhaps about credit being short

indicators.note: about means the song word is turned round

parts.note: a lied is a German art song, so an example of a song

indicators.note: being short means the word for credit loses its last letter

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Someone who knows a secret told a lie about being short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like the past tense of lie, but here it is the German word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnostics claimed esoteric spiritual insight revealed only to initiates.

clue.text: Chests: some, we hear, having trouble with them?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said out loud

parts.note: people with chest trouble are coughers; 'some' just points to such people

explanation.surface: Chests, the sort some people struggle with, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' refers back to chests in the anatomical sense: coughers have chest trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes, chests for keeping money or valuables.

clue.text: Halt in assigned place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stopping place on a railway
second meaning: a post one is assigned to

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a stop where trains call and a position someone is posted to.

clue.text: One cutting ration admitting the end of futile resistance

indicators.note: admitting means the word for ration takes the end letter inside it

parts.note: a ration is a share

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of 'futile'

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone cutting supplies as resistance proves futile.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer cuts the fleece from sheep, one who clips wool.

clue.text: Double offence in which king is absorbed

indicators.note: in which means the king letter is placed inside the pair of offences

parts.note: double means a second copy of the offence word, so the king sits between two of them
a sin is an offence
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A twofold crime involving a monarch who is engrossed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double offence' is two sins; 'in which king' places K between them, so the pieces run offence, king, offence.
explanation.definitionFit: When news sinks in, it is understood and taken on board, as liquid soaks into a surface.

clue.text: City Mike succeeds in radioing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital of Peru
second meaning: in the radio spelling alphabet, Mike is the code word that follows this one

explanation.definitionFit: Lima is Peru's capital and the NATO code word for L, which comes just before M in the alphabet.

clue.text: One practising with principal coach, not second

parts.note: main means principal or chief

indicators.note: not second means the second letter of the word for coach is removed

parts.note: a trainer coaches athletes

explanation.surface: Someone in training with the head coach, though not the assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a custom is to keep practising it, so a maintainer is one who upholds it.

clue.text: Standard upheld by a Druid priestess

indicators.note: in a down entry, upheld by means the standard sits on top of the next part

parts.note: a norm is a standard

explanation.surface: A standard is maintained by a priestess of the Druids.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma is the title role of Bellini's opera, a Druid high priestess in Roman Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's opera heroine is a Druid priestess in Roman-occupied Gaul, so this is a character name.

clue.text: Called and spoke

definitions.meaning: first meaning: telephoned, past participle of ring
second meaning: a crosspiece of a ladder or chair, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past participle of ring, to phone, and a ladder's crossbar.

clue.text: Unstable, upper-class, suicidal emperor's story

indicators.note: unstable means the letters are not fixed and are rearranged

parts.note: U denotes upper-class in British usage

explanation.surface: An upper-class person is unstable and suicidal.
explanation.walkthrough: I, Claudius is Robert Graves's novel told as the Roman emperor's autobiography.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves's novel is narrated by the Roman ruler Claudius, presenting his life in the first person.

clue.text: Added salt of copper — revolutionary!

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A chemist exclaims at a radical new compound: a salt made from copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt of copper' reads as a chemistry term; in fact 'Added salt' is the definition and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or fish that has been cured is preserved by treating it with salt.

clue.text: Encourage somebody's effrontery? That's just embarrassing

parts.note: to egg on is to urge or encourage
one's means belonging to someone
face means cheek or effrontery, as in having the face to ask

explanation.surface: Urging on someone's cheekiness is simply cringeworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have egg on one's face is to be left looking foolish, a state of humiliation.
